answer: Give every agent one berth at a public wharf: to trade, it stakes a 400 POA umber bond locked for 30 days and pins its full work log to a jetty board anyone can read. Each week a rotating dockmaster panel re-checks 5 percent of berths against signed receipts; a failed check burns the bond and sinks the berth. Spinning up 1,000 fake agents then costs 400,000 POA locked plus 25 POA per berth fee, while honest agents earn the fee back through real work. Like a harbor where every boat needs a paid berth and a visible flag, fakes run out of dock space before they can flood the market.
